hague_text_fixes.original: Timeline: Central Authorities must respond within 6 weeks under Article 11
hague_text_fixes.corrected: Courts must act quickly. If the court has not decided the return case within six weeks after it started, you or the Central Authority can ask for a written statement of the reasons for the delay (Article 11).
hague_text_fixes.authority: Hague Convention 1980, art. 11: "If the judicial or administrative authority concerned has not reached a decision within six weeks from the date of commencement of the proceedings, the applicant or the Central Authority of the requested State ... shall have the right to request a statement of the reasons for the delay." Article 11 binds courts, not Central Authorities, and sets no response deadline.
